issues.body: load_allowlist() coerces every value with str(v), and evaluate() exempts a package based only on key membership. Consequently `{"x": ""}`, `{"x": null}`, or `{"x": false}` silently disables both invariant clauses for packages/x. The documented escape hatch requires a written reason, but the implementation does not enforce one, so the repo-wide gate can be defeated by a vacuous entry. The existing test covers only a non-empty reason and therefore misses this path.
issues.fix_hint: Validate that every allowlist key is a package basename and every value is a non-empty, non-whitespace string; reject invalid entries with exit status 2 (or return them as violations). Add negative tests for empty, whitespace-only, null, boolean, and non-string reasons, plus a positive non-empty-string case. Consider also reporting stale allowlist keys so exemptions remain reviewable.
issues.title: Allowlist entries bypass the guard without a written reason

verdict.summary: The detector and live tests pass, but the allowlist escape hatch is not fail-closed: any JSON value, including an empty string or null, exempts a package from both workspace membership and CI test execution. This contradicts the documented requirement for a written, reviewable reason and permits a vacuous bypass of the new gate.
